paraphrase: Sukhāvatī: its beings know no suffering, only joys; it has seven rows of railings, jewel-trees, ponds of the eight virtues with lotuses as large as cartwheels, and birds conjured by Amitābha whose songs proclaim the faculties, powers and limbs of awakening, so that all who hear them recollect the Buddha, dharma and saṅgha.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: One cannot be born in that land with few good roots and little merit: a good man or woman who hears of Amitābha and holds fast to his name for one day, or up to seven days, with a mind undistracted, will see Amitābha and the holy assembly before them at the end of life, and dying without confusion will be born in Sukhāvatī.

original.text: 聞說阿彌陀佛，執持名號，若一日、若二日、若三日、若四日、若五日、若六日、若七日，一心不亂。

paraphrase: The buddhas of the six directions, numberless as the Ganges' sands, extend their tongues over the trichiliocosm and testify to the truth of this teaching, 'protected and borne in mind by all buddhas'.
